normalized.governing_thought: Raise prices in 2027 where customers stay: 12% for mid-market, enterprise up to its caps, and SMB only after a test
executive_summary: Rising churn comes from 2025 promotion customers reaching full price: they explain 91% of the SMB rise – SMB churn outside the promotion moved only from 2.0% to 2.1% a month (p. 5–10)
Mid-market has shown it will pay more and enterprise rarely leaves, but SMB pricing is unproven with Inkwell at $9 – Our SMB win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year (p. 12–16)
The CFO's 12% can add only $7.6M in 2027, and mid-market and enterprise rises alone clear the $98.9M target – Without any SMB rise, 2027 ARR still reaches about $99.03M (p. 18–23)

Activation is the lever on the promotion cohort's churn, but fixing it cuts SMB churn by up to a third, not half – Only 41% of promotion customers activated in month one, against 72% elsewhere (p. 25–28)
Approve in December, raise mid-market and enterprise from January, and decide SMB in July – A Q1 test of +8% on non-promotion SMB renewals gates the July decision (p. 30–34)

slides.title: Pricing in 2027 while churn rises
Key questions

claims.claim: Should Palisade raise prices at 2027 renewals while churn rises, and if so where and by how much, to grow ARR 15% with retention above 100%?
evidence: Decision maker: CEO, with the leadership team, approving the 2027 pricing plan
Success criteria: ARR grows at least 15% in 2027, from $86.0M; Net revenue retention stays above 100% overall; Each price move rests on evidence for that segment
Timing: Leadership meeting, December 2026
Out of scope: New plans, such as a low-cost SMB tier; Enterprise contracts before renewal; New-customer sales targets

Sub-questions: 1 Where is churn rising, and is price the cause? 2 Which customers will accept a higher price in 2027? 3 What does each option add to 2027 ARR, and does it pass the 15% growth and 100% retention tests? 4 What will bring SMB churn down? 5 How do we roll the plan out in 2027, and what tells us it is working?

evidence: SMB churn outside the promotion moved only from 2.0% to 2.1% a month

evidence: Our SMB win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year
